messages.content: How do you rebuild self-trust after making a really bad decision?
Slowly, and mostly through small consistent proof rather than one big gesture. What kind of decision are we talking about, if you're comfortable sharing?
I ignored a lot of warning signs in a relationship and it cost me a lot.

That's a hard lesson but also a genuinely useful one going forward. Self-trust rebuilds by noticing warning signs early next time and actually acting on them, even small ones — each time you do that, you're proving to yourself you can be trusted with your own judgment again.
